bull_bear.body: Demerger of sugar business to unlock value and focus capital on Alco-Bev; Inorganic M&A under exploration for brand portfolio (domestic/international); Scotland distillery project in early stages (land/licenses secured).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on 60-70% growth guidance; Regulatory changes in state excise policies; Input cost volatility (grain, glass, fuel); Competition in INR 4,000-5,000 single malt segment; High working capital cycle (DSO 80-90 days).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, aggressive on growth targets, transparent about one-off margin pressures, strategic focus on global branding and pure-play spirits exposure.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Company does not sell bulk malt despite capacity increase; all malt is reserved for own premium bottling; Scotland distillery project is in works but not yet operational; Auditor change is partner-led continuity (Krishnan Mangwa moving to new firm) rather than governance issue.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Growth is framed as both organic and inorganic: "We plan to capitalise organic and inorganic growth opportunities" and "Exploring inorganic growth opportunities in other spirit categories".
- Journey timeline records a "Fund raise and capacity expansion commenced" milestone in 2024; the deck does not discuss dividends, buybacks, debt levels or a balance sheet.
- Ongoing reinvestment is directed at barrels (to 100,000 by March 2027), maturation warehousing, the Scotland distillery and a consumer-facing Indri Experience Centre built "with scalability to support future brand growth".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated manufacturing across sugar, distillery (ENA/ethanol) and premium spirits; the AR notes businesses with such integrated operations are better placed to benefit from evolving market opportunities while reducing the cyclicality traditionally associated with the sugar business
- Award-winning premium and luxury brand portfolio (Indri, Camikara, Whistler, Cashmir) with multiple international awards and recognitions that have enhanced its position in the global single malt category
- Raw-material integration from the sugar business into the distillery and premium spirits value chain
- In-house maturation and warehousing infrastructure, with barrels under maturation rising to 83,800 in FY26 from 75,000 in FY25
- Distribution reach across several Indian states and union territories, the CSD network and international markets
- Craft-led malt manufacturing process using rain-fed six-row non-GMO barley from Bundi, Rajasthan and double distillation in Scottish copper pot stills, with no artificial colouring and no chill filtration for standard expressions
- Premium-led mix shift, with the distillery business recording a 31.5% EBITDA margin in FY 2025-26 versus 19.3% in FY22
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material cost volatility — The AR's material-risk table states that variations in barley, sugarcane and molasses prices can affect production costs and margins, as raw materials remain one of the largest components of the Company's cost structure. Mitigation cited: diversified sourcing across multiple regions, long-term procurement arrangements, a resilient supply network and an increasing contribution from premium products with stronger margin profiles.
- State excise policy and regulatory complexity — Variations in state regulations may affect pricing approvals, product registrations, market access and product launches. Mitigation cited: dedicated compliance teams, advance label registrations, engagement with industry bodies and a diversified market presence across multiple states.
- Capital project execution — Large-scale capacity expansion projects involve construction, commissioning, regulatory and operational risks. The AR notes the Indri expansion and Chhattisgarh facility were commissioned within planned timelines and budgets during FY26, while the Scotland distillery project remains under active oversight; mitigation is phased investment planning, milestone-linked execution, independent project oversight and regular review.
- Capacity utilisation and market absorption after the recent expansions — Listed among the emerging risks under active monitoring — whether the newly commissioned capacity is utilised and absorbed by the market is an open question following the recent expansion projects.
- Brand integrity and counterfeiting — As the premium brands gain wider recognition, exposure to imitation, counterfeiting and reputational risk also increases. Mitigation cited: product authentication measures, trademark protection, market monitoring and participation in industry initiatives that support category standards and safeguard the integrity of Indian Single Malt Whisky.
- Talent and organisational scaling — Business expansion increases demand for specialised manufacturing, commercial and leadership talent. Mitigation cited: strengthened leadership capabilities, employee ownership programmes, structured onboarding and development initiatives for technical and commercial roles.
- Evolving regulatory standards and trade policy for Indian spirits — Under active monitoring as emerging risks: potential implications of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement on the premium spirits category, evolving regulatory standards and product definitions for Indian spirits, and the proposed Geographical Indication protection for Indian Single Malt Whisky.
- Changing consumer preferences towards health, wellness and moderation — Named in the emerging risk landscape as an external development that may influence the business, the premium spirits category and the broader industry — a structural demand risk for an alcoholic beverages producer.
- Pending employee and worker litigation — The BRSR NGRBC complaints table shows 43 employee and worker complaints pending resolution at the close of both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, remarked as 'Court cases', with 4 filed during FY 2025-26. No nature, forum or quantum is disclosed. Separately, the BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table is returned as NIL, so the AR discloses no material ESG risk of its own there.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as "India's largest independent producer of malt spirits", with a portfolio spanning single malt whisky, cane juice rum, vodka and IMFL brands, plus Ethanol, ENA, DDGS and white crystal sugar.
- Indri is claimed as the "top selling Indian Single Malt globally and India" and "Largest selling Single Malt in India, for two consecutive years" (2024, 2025), and "amongst top 15 Single Malts globally".
- Awards are presented as the validation mechanism: 191 total awards won since 2022 (Indri 139, Camikara 41, Cashmir 8, Whistler 3), including 50 awards in Q1 and "Best Indian Distillery of the Year" at the Tokyo Whisky & Spirits Competition 2026.
- Product-level moat claims: Indri's triple wood maturation and Himalayan terroir at Indri, Haryana ("a profile no competitor replicates"); Camikara as "India's First Pure Cane Juice Rum" (cane juice, not molasses); Cashmir distilled from Sona Moti, a revived 2,000-year-old heirloom Indian wheat.
- First to introduce the Indian Malt Whisky Association (IMWA) certification hologram on its bottles, positioned as an authenticity/credibility marker for Indian single malt.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] "Scheme of arrangement for Sugar business was filed with the Stock Exchanges on 28.4.2026 and is work in progress" — implying a separation of the sugar vertical from the distillery business.
- [Certification] First to introduce the IMWA certification hologram on Indri Single Malt bottles, certifying adherence to IMWA production standards and category integrity.
- [ESOP] Employee benefits expense includes an ESOP charge of Rs. 2.47 Cr for the quarter.
- [Market opportunity] Deck cites (S&P Global market intelligence / IWSR-based management estimates, 9-litre cases) India Spirits 420 Mn (2025) to 560 Mn (2030F) at ~6% CAGR; Indian Single Malt 0.53 Mn to 0.78 Mn at ~8%; Aged Premium Rum 34K to 77K at ~18%; Vodka 0.55 Mn to 0.97 Mn at ~12%.
- [Channel] CSD and Paramilitary institutional channels remain a stated focus for branded products, alongside 16 Indian and 19 international duty free outlets.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company is an integrated alcoholic beverage (alcobev) manufacturer that also produces other distillery products including ENA and ethanol, and operates a sugar business. Established as a sugar manufacturing enterprise in Haryana, it diversified into distillery operations and built a differentiated portfolio of premium and luxury spirits brands sold across Indian states and union territories, the CSD network and international markets. It supplies its alcohol products to contractors, dealers and import agencies, sells ENA to third-party beverage manufacturers and captively, and supplies fuel-grade ethanol under the Government of India's Ethanol Blended Petrol programme.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **IMFL / branded alcobev:** Indri Single Malt Whisky, Indri Trini, Indri Dru, Indri Agneya, Indri City Series (Mumbai, Bengaluru, Dubai editions), Indri Diwali Collector's Edition, Indri Founder's Reserve Series, Indri Rudhira, Camikara Rum, Camikara 3-Year Aged Rum, Camikara Expressions, Whistler Blended Malt Whisky, Whistler Premium Whisky Range, Cashmir Premium Vodka
- **Other distillery:** Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), Ethanol (fuel grade, under EBP programme), Malt Spirit, DDGS, IMIL, B2B Malt
- **Sugar:** Plantation white sugar

outlook.body: N/A for FMCG; Demand visibility strong with supply constraints now resolved; Malt inventory built up to INR 100 Cr to support future bottling.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Chhattisgarh plant to contribute INR 300-400 Cr in FY27; Indri plant expansion to add INR 250-300 Cr; New product pipeline (premium/luxury extensions) kicking in Q1 FY27; Target to become top 5 global single malt brand in 3-5 years; Exports target 50% of revenue in 3-5 years.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Centre strategic direction on the branded alcobev/IMFL and other distillery businesses, which management describes as the most significant opportunities for value creation, while the sugar business continues to contribute
- Demerge the sugar business into a separate entity — the Board approved the proposed demerger and a scheme of arrangement was filed with the stock exchanges on April 28, 2026 — to give both businesses sharper strategic focus and let investors participate directly in each
- Premiumisation as the core philosophy, with focus on higher-end luxury products and on building enduring brands rather than pursuing short-term volume growth
- Span multiple high-end premium, luxury and super-luxury categories through Indri, Camikara, Cashmir and Whistler, each built around a distinct identity and consumer proposition
- Continue investing in quality, innovation and ageing inventory, and build maturation/barrel capacity as a prerequisite for sustained leadership in premium spirits
- Expand presence across India and international markets, deepening retail, on-trade and duty-free distribution
- Use the completed Indri and Mahasamund expansions to cater to branded alcobev/IMFL products, utilising the capacity for ENA and ethanol in the interim
- Build an international manufacturing presence at Portavadie, Scotland to access whisky-making expertise, technology, talent and the global whisky ecosystem, with more opportunities unfolding as the UK FTA becomes operational
- Pursue both organic and inorganic opportunities that strengthen the portfolio and enhance long-term shareholder value
- Strengthen leadership and operational capability through senior and middle-level appointments across manufacturing, supply chain and human resources
- Deepen consumer engagement through experiential assets such as the Indri Experience Centre inaugurated at the Haryana distillery during the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26 the Company completed significant investments in Haryana and Chhattisgarh: the expansion at the Indri distillery and the setting up of a greenfield distillery in Chhattisgarh were both completed during the year. The Indri expansion raised ENA and ethanol capacity from 78 KLPD to 220 KLPD and malt spirit capacity from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD, and additional maturation and warehousing infrastructure was commissioned to support future requirements; the AR's scaling-production-capacity summary shows combined ENA/ethanol capacity moving from 78 KLPD earlier to 420 KLPD currently and malt spirit from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD. The greenfield 200 KLPD ENA and ethanol facility at Mahasamund, Chhattisgarh was commissioned during FY2025-26 and establishes a manufacturing presence in central India, supporting ENA for IMFL blending, country liquor and bulk sales and ethanol for oil marketing companies, while providing a platform for future IMIL and IMFL launches; the Company also plans to launch IMFL products there and calls it key to its strategy for national expansion. At Indri the Company plans to launch more IMFL products and is modernising and expanding bottling capacity, and states that enhanced capacity in manufacturing, storage and maturation will lead to adequate supply for achieving its long-term goals for Indri and other ultra-luxury products. Maturation capacity is described as a critical part of long-term strategy: barrels under maturation rose to 83,800 in FY26 from 75,000 in FY25 (45,000 in FY24 and 33,000 in FY23), and the Company is targeting an inventory of 100,000 barrels with corresponding maturation halls by March 2027. Internationally, the proposed malt distillery at Portavadie, Scotland is the Company's first international manufacturing investment; board approval, land acquisition, statutory approvals and funding arrangements have been completed, and with the UK FTA becoming operational options are being evaluated. No rupee quantum for any of these projects is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural transformation of the Indian alcoholic beverages industry, with consumers moving beyond volume-led mass consumption towards products offering premium quality and experience
- Rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and an expanding aspirational consumer base reshaping consumption patterns in India
- Indian Single Malt market projected to grow at approximately 8% CAGR through 2030, with premium rum and vodka segments growing faster than the broader market
- More than 100 million consumers expected to reach legal drinking age in India over the next five years; India's spirits market estimated at 424 million cases and projected at 560 million cases by 2030
- Mix shift towards branded IMFL lifting earnings quality — the distillery segment recorded EBITDA margins of 31.5% in FY 2025-26, which management says is among the highest in the listed alcoholic beverage segment, against 19.3% in FY22
- IMFL portfolio volume growth of 48% during the year, with Whistler growing 98% and Indri and Camikara continuing to scale; distillery segment revenue grew 41.7%
- Distribution expansion: products available across 29 states and union territories in India through more than 25,000 relevant retail and on-trade outlets, and brands present across 32 countries and 35 duty-free locations
- Brand equity from international recognition — over 141 international awards across the portfolio, including Best World Whisky for Indri's Diwali Collector's Edition 2025 at the Las Vegas Global Spirits Awards with a score of 99.1
- Total distillery capacity raised to 450 KLPD after the Indri expansion and the Mahasamund greenfield commissioning, providing a platform for future growth
- The expanded Indri facility is expected to contribute meaningfully from FY 2026-27 onwards; the Chhattisgarh facility, initially focused on ENA and ethanol, will ramp up IMFL production over the coming years
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Piccadily Agro crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26 driven by premium IMFL brands, with a strategic demerger of the low-margin sugar business to focus purely on high-growth spirits. Guidance for 60-70% growth in FY27 is underpinned by the full monetization of new 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh capacity and resolved supply constraints at the Indri plant.

currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the Company completed significant investments in Haryana and Chhattisgarh: the expansion at the Indri distillery and the setting up of a greenfield distillery in Chhattisgarh were both completed during the year. The Indri expansion raised ENA and ethanol capacity from 78 KLPD to 220 KLPD and malt spirit capacity from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD, and additional maturation and warehousing infrastructure was commissioned to support future requirements; the AR's scaling-production-capacity summary shows combined ENA/ethanol capacity moving from 78 KLPD earlier to 420 KLPD currently and malt spirit from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD. At Indri the Company plans to launch more IMFL products and is modernising and expanding bottling capacity, and states that enhanced capacity in manufacturing, storage and maturation will lead to adequate supply for achieving its long-term goals for Indri and other ultra-luxury products. Maturation capacity is described as a critical part of long-term strategy: barrels under maturation rose to 83,800 in FY26 from 75,000 in FY25 (45,000 in FY24 and 33,000 in FY23), and the Company is targeting an inventory of 100,000 barrels with corresponding maturation halls by March 2027. Internationally, the proposed malt distillery at Portavadie, Scotland is the Company's first international manufacturing investment; board approval, land acquisition, statutory approvals and funding arrangements have been completed, and with the UK FTA becoming operational options are being evaluated. No rupee quantum for any of these projects is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.note: The AR's material-risk table states that variations in barley, sugarcane and molasses prices can affect production costs and margins, as raw materials remain one of the largest components of the Company's cost structure. Mitigation cited: diversified sourcing across multiple regions, long-term procurement arrangements, a resilient supply network and an increasing contribution from premium products with stronger margin profiles.

risks.risk: State excise policy and regulatory complexity
risks.note: Variations in state regulations may affect pricing approvals, product registrations, market access and product launches. Mitigation cited: dedicated compliance teams, advance label registrations, engagement with industry bodies and a diversified market presence across multiple states.

Large-scale capacity expansion projects involve construction, commissioning, regulatory and operational risks. The AR notes the Indri expansion and Chhattisgarh facility were commissioned within planned timelines and budgets during FY26, while the Scotland distillery project remains under active oversight; mitigation is phased investment planning, milestone-linked execution, independent project oversight and regular review.

risks.risk: Capacity utilisation and market absorption after the recent expansions
risks.note: Listed among the emerging risks under active monitoring — whether the newly commissioned capacity is utilised and absorbed by the market is an open question following the recent expansion projects.

As the premium brands gain wider recognition, exposure to imitation, counterfeiting and reputational risk also increases. Mitigation cited: product authentication measures, trademark protection, market monitoring and participation in industry initiatives that support category standards and safeguard the integrity of Indian Single Malt Whisky.

Business expansion increases demand for specialised manufacturing, commercial and leadership talent. Mitigation cited: strengthened leadership capabilities, employee ownership programmes, structured onboarding and development initiatives for technical and commercial roles.

risks.risk: Evolving regulatory standards and trade policy for Indian spirits
risks.note: Under active monitoring as emerging risks: potential implications of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement on the premium spirits category, evolving regulatory standards and product definitions for Indian spirits, and the proposed Geographical Indication protection for Indian Single Malt Whisky.

risks.risk: Changing consumer preferences towards health, wellness and moderation
risks.note: Named in the emerging risk landscape as an external development that may influence the business, the premium spirits category and the broader industry — a structural demand risk for an alcoholic beverages producer.

The BRSR NGRBC complaints table shows 43 employee and worker complaints pending resolution at the close of both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, remarked as 'Court cases', with 4 filed during FY 2025-26. No nature, forum or quantum is disclosed. Separately, the BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table is returned as NIL, so the AR discloses no material ESG risk of its own there.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Piccadily Agro Industries is an integrated alcobev, distillery (ENA/ethanol) and sugar manufacturer that has become a leading player in India's premium spirits segment, with IMFL revenue of INR 502 crore in FY26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is an integrated alcoholic beverage (alcobev) manufacturer that also produces other distillery products including ENA and ethanol, and operates a sugar business. Established as a sugar manufacturing enterprise in Haryana, it diversified into distillery operations and built a differentiated portfolio of premium and luxury spirits brands sold across Indian states and union territories, the CSD network and international markets. It supplies its alcohol products to contractors, dealers and import agencies, sells ENA to third-party beverage manufacturers and captively, and supplies fuel-grade ethanol under the Government of India's Ethanol Blended Petrol programme.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural transformation of the Indian alcoholic beverages industry, with consumers moving beyond volume-led mass consumption towards products offering premium quality and experience
- Rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanisation and an expanding aspirational consumer base reshaping consumption patterns in India
- Indian Single Malt market projected to grow at approximately 8% CAGR through 2030, with premium rum and vodka segments growing faster than the broader market
- More than 100 million consumers expected to reach legal drinking age in India over the next five years; India's spirits market estimated at 424 million cases and projected at 560 million cases by 2030
- Mix shift towards branded IMFL lifting earnings quality — the distillery segment recorded EBITDA margins of 31.5% in FY 2025-26, which management says is among the highest in the listed alcoholic beverage segment, against 19.3% in FY22
- IMFL portfolio volume growth of 48% during the year, with Whistler growing 98% and Indri and Camikara continuing to scale; distillery segment revenue grew 41.7%
- Distribution expansion: products available across 29 states and union territories in India through more than 25,000 relevant retail and on-trade outlets, and brands present across 32 countries and 35 duty-free locations
- Brand equity from international recognition — over 141 international awards across the portfolio, including Best World Whisky for Indri's Diwali Collector's Edition 2025 at the Las Vegas Global Spirits Awards with a score of 99.1
- Total distillery capacity raised to 450 KLPD after the Indri expansion and the Mahasamund greenfield commissioning, providing a platform for future growth
- The expanded Indri facility is expected to contribute meaningfully from FY 2026-27 onwards; the Chhattisgarh facility, initially focused on ENA and ethanol, will ramp up IMFL production over the coming years

The Indri expansion raised ENA and ethanol capacity from 78 KLPD to 220 KLPD and malt spirit capacity from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD, and additional maturation and warehousing infrastructure was commissioned to support future requirements; the AR's scaling-production-capacity summary shows combined ENA/ethanol capacity moving from 78 KLPD earlier to 420 KLPD currently and malt spirit from 12 KLPD to 30 KLPD. The greenfield 200 KLPD ENA and ethanol facility at Mahasamund, Chhattisgarh was commissioned during FY2025-26 and establishes a manufacturing presence in central India, supporting ENA for IMFL blending, country liquor and bulk sales and ethanol for oil marketing companies, while providing a platform for future IMIL and IMFL launches; the Company also plans to launch IMFL products there and calls it key to its strategy for national expansion. At Indri the Company plans to launch more IMFL products and is modernising and expanding bottling capacity, and states that enhanced capacity in manufacturing, storage and maturation will lead to adequate supply for achieving its long-term goals for Indri and other ultra-luxury products. Maturation capacity is described as a critical part of long-term strategy: barrels under maturation rose to 83,800 in FY26 from 75,000 in FY25 (45,000 in FY24 and 33,000 in FY23), and the Company is targeting an inventory of 100,000 barrels with corresponding maturation halls by March 2027. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturing across sugar, distillery (ENA/ethanol) and premium spirits; the AR notes businesses with such integrated operations are better placed to benefit from evolving market opportunities while reducing the cyclicality traditionally associated with the sugar business
- Award-winning premium and luxury brand portfolio (Indri, Camikara, Whistler, Cashmir) with multiple international awards and recognitions that have enhanced its position in the global single malt category
- Raw-material integration from the sugar business into the distillery and premium spirits value chain
- In-house maturation and warehousing infrastructure, with barrels under maturation rising to 83,800 in FY26 from 75,000 in FY25
- Distribution reach across several Indian states and union territories, the CSD network and international markets
- Craft-led malt manufacturing process using rain-fed six-row non-GMO barley from Bundi, Rajasthan and double distillation in Scottish copper pot stills, with no artificial colouring and no chill filtration for standard expressions
- Premium-led mix shift, with the distillery business recording a 31.5% EBITDA margin in FY 2025-26 versus 19.3% in FY22

risks.body: Execution risk on 60-70% growth guidance; Regulatory changes in state excise policies; Input cost volatility (grain, glass, fuel); Competition in INR 4,000-5,000 single malt segment; High working capital cycle (DSO 80-90 days).

non_obvious.body: Company does not sell bulk malt despite capacity increase; all malt is reserved for own premium bottling; Scotland distillery project is in works but not yet operational; Auditor change is partner-led continuity (Krishnan Mangwa moving to new firm) rather than governance issue.
